Lessons.Title: Relate Quotients to Familiar Products
ExplanationParagraphs: Known multiplication products can help solve related division facts: if a×b=c and neither factor is zero, then c÷a=b and c÷b=a.
Original warm-up Number Talk uses precisely4×10,40÷4,40÷10 and60÷6. Answers40,10,4,10 show the connections. Explain each mentally, not just tally scores.

Original Card Sort Multiplication (20min) uses partner-prepared cards from a blackline master. Pupils classify each card as 'know it right away', 'can find it quickly' or 'don't know it yet'; they choose FIVE personal facts to practice with a partner, finding strategies. These bins are not fixed numeric-answer grades. The exact source blackline cards were not reproduced.

Original Activity2 If I Know, Then I Know (15min) reuses the card pile. Public source example: If4×5=20 then20÷4=5 and20÷5=4. Each pupil draws a card and creates one multiplication and two division equations; the chosen cards are not predetermined, and teacher checks family relationships.
Independently authored extra skill examples6×7=42 gives42÷6=7 and42÷7=6;3×8=24 gives24÷3=8 and24÷8=3. These were not source publisher card statements.

Lesson synthesis: knowing the product of two factors supports division with either factor as the divisor. For square facts such as5×5=25 the two forms coincide numerically; there is no fabricated distinct answer.

Source 2021 third-party photo, original multiplication card blackline/paper, original PDF and gated Multiplication and Division Facts Cool-down are outside evidence. Edulytics companion is first-party skill-aligned authoring; no tests or Stage D were run.

KeyConcepts.Title: Fact family
KeyConcepts.Definition: Multiplication product and two related division equations.

KeyConcepts.Title: Personal fluency check
KeyConcepts.Definition: Learner self-sorts known, quickly derived, and unfamiliar multiplication facts.
KeyConcepts.Rule: No universal correct fluency category for all learners.
KeyConcepts.Example: One learner might know6×7 instantly; another practices it.

KeyConcepts.Title: Practice five facts
KeyConcepts.Definition: Choose five self-identified less familiar products to review with teacher/partner.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Try known doubles, fives, tens, decomposition and array reasoning.

WorkedExamples.Title: Known product 4×5
WorkedExamples.Question: If 4×5=20, what related quotients follow?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the product and each factor as divisor in turn.

WorkedExamples.Title: Known product 6×7
WorkedExamples.Question: If 6×7=42, what related quotients follow?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the product and each factor as divisor in turn.

WorkedExamples.Title: Known product 3×8
WorkedExamples.Question: If 3×8=24, what related quotients follow?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the product and each factor as divisor in turn.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use a universally fixed correct sorting category for every multiplication card.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original assesses each pupil's personal fluency.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher validates honest self-assessment and strategies rather than a model-generated label.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat a correct multiplication product as only one possible division fact.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Each factor can act as divisor, producing an unknown other factor.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claim practice facts are original source card statements.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Exact publisher blackline card set not inspected.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Mark sample fact pairs as first-party equivalents.

SummaryPoints: Original Activity1 pupil sorts personal multiplication facts and selects five to improve.
Publisher card pixels/gated Cool-down unverified; Stage D not started.
